purpose: Licensed intentional divergences across the SDK/CLI/MCP surfaces: schema kinds (extra-param, widened-type, name-for-id, omitted-param) plus the cross-surface behavior kind. Every divergence a checker can observe must carry a license entry here; an unlicensed divergence reds, and a license entry with no matching divergence in the code (rot) reds too, in both directions. This file was created ahead of its checker (P6); scripts/check-mcp-schema-parity.mjs landed with W2 in two halves: W2a (this batch) licenses the widened-type coercion family and emits the parameter-level schema artifact; W2b (a later item) adds the full per-operation extra/omitted-param diff -- a naive per-instance diff produces hundreds of false positives from request-body fields and universal dry_run/confirm_token write-confirmation params that need family-level rules, not per-call-site licenses, so that half is deliberately deferred rather than landed half-verified.

entries.operationOrFamily: every MCP tool parameter built with zStringList(...) or zNumberLike(...)
entries.reason: mcp/src/arg-shapes.ts's zStringList/zNumberLike wrap a field in z.preprocess so the server also accepts a bare string where the wire type is an array ("x" => ["x"]) or a numeric string where the wire type is a number ("40.5" => 40.5) -- forgiving model-emitted arguments. This is a single family license, not one entry per call site (205 call sites across mcp/src/tools/**/*.ts at licensing time, dominated by the page/pageSize pagination pair on nearly every list tool): the MCP SDK's zod-to-json-schema conversion unwraps z.preprocess to the INNER schema, so the model-visible tool schema in docs/mcp-tool-schemas.json already reports the canonical array/number type -- only the server's runtime acceptance widens, and it widens identically everywhere the two helpers are used.

The CLI's delete command for an active project or client archives it first, then deletes, via wrapper/ensure.ts's archiveThenDelete core (archiveThenDeleteProject / archiveThenDeleteClient) -- the Clockify API rejects deleting an active project or client directly. SDK and MCP callers building on the raw API surface do not get this chain automatically; only the CLI's delete command wires it in. (Tasks do not have this chain; an earlier plan draft named tasks alongside projects/clients -- verified against the current cli/src/commands/*.ts and corrected here.)

entries.operationOrFamily: name-for-id resolver family (every tool accepting a name in an id slot)
entries.reason: When a resolver name-to-id lookup is ambiguous or unknown, the MCP surface returns a grounded clarification receipt (real candidate ids, a question, and it never reaches the write or list API) instead of guessing or failing opaquely. SDK and CLI resolvers do not have this stop -- they either resolve deterministically or throw.

entries.operationOrFamily: risky write tools (business writes, external side effects, privileged writes, destructive writes)
entries.reason: Every MCP tool whose confirmation metadata is preview_token requires a dry_run call first, returning a confirm_token bound to a hash of the preview and the business args; the real write is refused without a matching, unexpired, unused token. SDK and CLI writes execute directly with no preview/confirm handshake.
